record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine the exact dilation of the five vertices of a regular pentagon in the plane.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 19. What is the dilation of the vertices of a regular 5-gon? It is known that this dilation is at most 1.02046; see [34].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite point set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$, define the dilation (or stretch factor) of $S$ as
$$\Delta(S) \;=\; \inf_{G} \; \max_{p \neq q \in S} \; \frac{d_G(p,q)}{\|p-q\|_2},$$
where the infimum is taken over all finite plane (i.e. non-crossing) straight-line graphs $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ whose vertex set contains $S$, $d_G(p,q)$ denotes the length of a shortest path in $G$ between $p$ and $q$ (measured as the sum of Euclidean edge lengths), and $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the Euclidean norm. Edges of $G$ are straight-line segments and additional Steiner points are allowed.

Let $S_5 \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be the set of five vertices of a regular pentagon. Determine the exact value of $\Delta(S_5)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of determining the exact dilation of the five vertices of a regular pentagon appears to remain open. The best known upper bound for general regular polygons has been improved (e.g., to about 1.4482 for arbitrary regular n-gons), and a specific upper bound of 1.02046 is known for the pentagon, but no matching lower bound or exact value has been published. No source was found announcing a definitive solution.

status_evidence.title: An improved upper bound on dilation of regular polygons
status_evidence.snippet: An upper bound of 1.4482 on dilation of vertices of regular polygons was established by constructing a triangulation of a regular polygon...
status_evidence.claim: Recent work focuses on upper bounds for dilation of regular polygon vertices, indicating the exact value is still not established.

status_evidence.title: The Geometric Dilation of Three Points
status_evidence.snippet: Related geometric dilation problems for small point sets are studied.
status_evidence.claim: Dilation problems for small symmetric point sets in the plane remain an active topic without exact resolution for the regular pentagon.
